title: NanoClaw Coworkers
description: NanoClaw coworker fleet. Provisioned from the repo - edit the JSON, not the UI (canSave is false by design). Panels labelled (5m) read a server-side 5-minute rolling window and do not widen with the dashboard range.

panels.title: Containers running

targets.query: SELECT mean("sessions_running") FROM "nanoclaw_fleet" WHERE $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval) fill(previous)

panels.title: Silent failures & liveness (previously collected, never displayed)
Win rate

targets.query: SELECT last("issuePartition_winRate") FROM "nanoclaw_funnel" WHERE $timeFilter

panels.description: issuePartition_winRate from reports/funnel.json. Collected every minute since the funnel cron began; nothing has ever displayed it.

panels.title: Fleet silence (max)

targets.query: SELECT last("max_silence_sec") FROM "nanoclaw_fleet" WHERE $timeFilter

panels.description: Longest time any RUNNING container has gone without activity. The container 3h absolute ceiling is 10800s; a value approaching it means a container is idle-but-alive and will be SIGTERMed.

panels.title: Stale running containers

targets.query: SELECT last("stale_running") FROM "nanoclaw_fleet" WHERE $timeFilter

panels.description: Containers with container_status=running but silent for more than STALE_SEC (3600s). Liveness is not progress - this is the count that reads as healthy in every other view.

panels.title: Tool failures (5m)

targets.query: SELECT last("tool_failures") FROM "nanoclaw_fleet" WHERE $timeFilter

panels.description: PostToolUseFailure hook events in the current 5-minute window, fleet-wide.

panels.title: Funnel snapshot age

targets.query: SELECT last("age_sec") FROM "nanoclaw_funnel" WHERE $timeFilter

panels.description: Age of reports/funnel.json. The funnel timer runs every 6h, so a value far above ~21600s means the funnel cron has stopped and every funnel number on this dashboard is stale.

panels.title: Sessions running / active

targets.query: SELECT last("sessions_running") AS "running", last("sessions_active") AS "active", last("sessions_total") AS "total" FROM "nanoclaw_fleet" WHERE $timeFilter

panels.description: Fleet session counts. running = container up; active = session live; total = all rows.

panels.title: Win rate over time

targets.query: SELECT mean("issuePartition_winRate") FROM "nanoclaw_funnel" WHERE $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval) fill(none)

panels.description: Win rate as a series - THIS one does respect the dashboard time range. fill(none) so a collector gap renders as a break in the line, not as a drop to zero.

panels.title: Fleet silence & stale over time

targets.query: SELECT max("max_silence_sec") AS "max_silence_sec", max("stale_running") AS "stale_running" FROM "nanoclaw_fleet" WHERE $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval) fill(none)

panels.description: fill(none): a gap in collection must read as a GAP, never as zero silence and zero stale containers.

panels.title: Collector heartbeat (unix)

targets.query: SELECT last("heartbeat_unixtime") FROM "nanoclaw_fleet" WHERE $timeFilter

panels.description: THE WATCHDOG FOR THIS ENTIRE DASHBOARD. The collector writes this every 60s. If it stops, InfluxDB simply stops gaining points and last() keeps serving the final value forever - which is exactly how issuePartition_winRate sat at a stale 0 from 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-11 while looking current. Compare against wall clock; if this stops advancing, DISTRUST EVERY OTHER PANEL HERE.

panels.title: Running sessions silent > 2.5h

targets.query: SELECT last("silent_beyond_warn") FROM "nanoclaw_fleet" WHERE $timeFilter

panels.description: Running sessions whose last_active is older than CEILING_SEC - CEILING_WARN_SEC (9000s). Named for what it measures - SILENCE, not container age. On prod max_silence_sec reads ~59800s against a 10800s container ceiling, so sessions.last_active demonstrably does not track the container heartbeat that container-runner.ts kills on. Still a real signal: a running session nobody has heard from in over two and a half hours.

panels.title: Collector points written

targets.query: SELECT sum("points") FROM "nanoclaw_collector" WHERE $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval) fill(none)

panels.description: Points written per collector run, over the selected range. fill(none) so a stopped collector renders as a BREAK in the line rather than a plausible-looking zero.

panels.title: Model tier per coworker
panels.description: Each coworker's configured model tier, from container_configs (the value `ncl groups config update --model` writes, materialized to container.json and passed to the SDK as the query model). An empty Model means the group inherits the host/provider default, shown as tier 'default' rather than a guessed tier. Activity (5m) is the rolling hook-event count — an approximate turn/work proxy, NOT billed cost. Scan the Tier column for drift.

targets.query: SELECT last("events"), last("running"), last("tool_failures") FROM "nanoclaw_group" WHERE $timeFilter GROUP BY "group", "coworker_type", "tier", "model", "provider"

panels.title: Activity share by tier (5m)
panels.description: Sum of the 5m hook-event activity across all coworkers on each model tier (collector-side rollup, measurement nanoclaw_tier). Shows how the fleet's work splits across opus / sonnet / haiku / default. Activity is a turn/work proxy, not billed cost.

targets.query: SELECT last("events") FROM "nanoclaw_tier" WHERE $timeFilter GROUP BY "tier"

panels.title: Coworkers per tier
panels.description: How many coworkers are configured on each model tier right now (nanoclaw_tier.coworkers). Makes tiering drift obvious: if a coworker flips opus↔sonnet, the bar counts move.

targets.query: SELECT last("coworkers") FROM "nanoclaw_tier" WHERE $timeFilter GROUP BY "tier"
